findings.body:
`fetchUser` now passes `{ timeout: 250 }` on the `http.get` call. The PR title/description present this as a move-only restructure, but 250ms is an aggressive network deadline for `/users/${id}` and will fail ordinary slow responses (multi-region RTT, cold upstream, brief GC pauses).

Either drop the timeout from this rename PR, or justify and tune it (and document the new SLA) as an intentional behavior change separate from the path move.

summary:
## Verdict

Behavior change is buried inside a path move: `fetchUser` now passes `{ timeout: 250 }` while the PR is framed as restructure-only.

## Notes

`src/a.ts` → `src/lib/a.ts` is a clean rename on disk. The only substantive edit is the new `timeout: 250` option on `http.get`. A 250ms budget is very tight for a `/users/:id` network call and will surface as intermittent failures under normal latency, cold starts, or distant regions.

No other files in this repo import `fetchUser`, so the path move itself has no in-tree call-site breakage to report. `http` is still an unresolved free identifier on both sides of the diff (pre-existing).

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: `src/lib/a.ts` defines `fetchUser` as `http.get(\`/users/${id}\`, { timeout: 250 })`, so the aggressive 250ms deadline is present on the network call as claimed. Nothing in the tree contradicts that behavior.
